extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals / writers who produce press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for writing press releases whose primary purpose is to generate reporter interest and media callbacks; includes when to use a release and when not to. Short tips-style how-to for PR practitioners and students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary goal: elicit a reporter callback
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release isn’t about clearing your desk or making the boss happy. It has just one goal: eliciting a call back from a reporter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame and write the press release with the single objective of prompting reporter interest and a follow-up call. Avoid letting internal convenience or administrative motives drive the release’s content or distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use press releases appropriately (don’t use them as a catch-all)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The press release is basically the butter knife of the PR writers’ toolkit,” says Long. “They end up dragging it out for everything in the world, and most of the time it’s a poor choice.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not default to issuing a press release for every minor task or request. Consider whether a release is the right tool to achieve media pickup; if the goal is internal housekeeping or pleasing a manager rather than attracting journalists, choose another approach.
